### Session b0d88998-e998-4b31-bcb8-c5fac8648084 - 2026-09-30T00:24:21.875Z

- User asked for full-year TMCP analysis instead of monthly snapshots to understand true visit frequency and pricing patterns, noting that seasonal peaks (like new jobs) distort monthly readings.
- Claude analyzed 272 mature TMCP jobs with complete 12-month visit history (Oct 1 – Sep 18) to establish stable baseline; counted all completed visits and scaled to annual patterns.
- Key finding: median 24 visits/year per job (16–32 range for middle 80%); seasonal swing from ~1.5/month (Feb–May) to 2.5–3/month (Jul, Oct); new jobs add only ~2 extra visits first two months, then normalize.
- Pricing audit revealed: $100/month correctly breaks even at ~34 visits/year; median job at 24 visits leaves 29% margin at $100; 258 jobs (35%) under $100 create pressure (avg $87, 21% margin, 26 unprofitable).
- Correction: prior analysis blamed the pricing formula; this read shows the formula is sound—profit weakness comes from older customers grandfathered at sub-$100 rates, not visit-frequency miscalculation.
- Recommendation: raise sub-$100 customers to $100 = ~$3.4K/month revenue (+$40K/year profit); sustainable if churn stays below ~13%.
